text:
asha: Heads up — saw a strange spike on canary last night. Traces show dozens of requests falling back from streaming safetensors chunked load to full fetch because the chunk header sig check failed. Latency jumped ~500ms for those calls.

mike: ouch. any idea if chunks actually corrupted or signature verification false-neg?

asha: looks like false-neg. We rolled out a change to the packer that started signing chunk headers with new key rotation metadata. Old loaders don't tolerate the extra field and treat it as verification failure.

liam: sketch of the header issue?

asha: header v1: {\n  id, offset, length, checksum\n}\nheader v2 (recent): {\n  id, offset, length, checksum, sig_meta\n}\nolder loader code checks for exact header layout bytes and bails.

mike: sigh. compatibility gap. two orthogonal problems: format evolution + expensive sig verification. We should avoid forcing verify on hot warmup path.

sora: is the sig itself on the chunk payload or on the header? if payload we can stream-verify incremental, if header-only quick verify.

asha: sig is header-signed (ed25519) and includes a small pubkey id and rotation epoch. Payloads left untouched. header sig verification is cheap-ish but still CPU and requires reading header bytes before deciding to stream.

liam: proposal: add namespacing fields (bundle_id, format_version, signing_epoch) into manifest and shard index. Loader should use manifest -> decide verifier strategy. That prevents arbitrary header field additions breaking older loaders.

mike: agree. Also add an opt-in verification API on WeightSource: `verify_header(header_bytes) -> enum {Trusted, Unverified, UnknownKey}`. Callers (runtime) can choose to skip verify during warmstart if manifest signals origin_trusted=true.

asha: +1. How about default behavior: hosted default OFF for signature verification during warmstart streaming; on-demand verify for integrity-sensitive customers?

eva: for Dedicated/Private we need a knob. Some compliance customers will mandate verification end-to-end. Make it config per deployment and per-route.

sora: tradeoff: if we skip verify on warmstart, we risk serving slightly faster but with potential supply-chain risk. Maybe permit deferred verification: stream responses to client but asynchronously verify shards and rollback if mismatch detected. That reduces tail latency.

mike: deferred verify is nice but adds complexity: need to track which outputs used unverified weights and have fast rollback path (evict weights, re-swap with verified shards). Also needs audit logs.

asha: right. We currently have an eviction + reload path but it's not tested under live inference. We should add a canary that simulates deferred-verify failures to validate rollback.

liam: on format evolution: require manifest to include `compatible_loader_min_version` and `header_schema_uri` (small JSON schema). Loaders should parse schema URIs they understand and ignore unknown optional fields under 'extensions'. No byte-exact checks.

mike: implementation notes:\n// WeightSource interface sketch\nclass WeightSource {\n  // fetch header bytes only\n  fetch_header(shard_id) -> bytes\n  // optional: verify header (may call KMS/HSM)\n  verify_header(header_bytes) -> \"Trusted\"|\"Unverified\"|\"UnknownKey\"\n  // fetch payload stream\n  stream_payload(shard_id) -> stream\n}\n
mike: cache verified pubkeys in in-memory LRU keyed by (bundle_id, signing_epoch) to avoid repeated KMS hits. Use batched verification when pulling many headers.

deploy-bot: CI: loading with `WEIGHT_VERIFY=1` shows +18% CPU on loader in unit tests, and one test timed out (prefetch smoke). Logs: `prefetch: header verify timeout 200ms`

asha: good to know. we'll need to tune timeouts and ensure forward-compat parsing avoids blocking on unknown fields.

eva: KMS note: ed25519 keys can't be paged through cloud-kms easily for high-throughput sign checks. We should support a local trusted key cache (rotated from KMS) for per-node verify to avoid per-request KMS call.

liam: and add key-proof-of-rotation metadata signed by KMS for offline verification. That way loader can trust a cached key until expiry.

sora: warmup tweak: add `warmup_mode: fast|safe|deferred_verify`. fast = no verify, safe = verify inline, deferred_verify = stream + async verify. Default hosted = deferred_verify? Or fast?

mike: deferred_verify seems like a reasonable default for hosted to balance latency and integrity, but must be opt-out for customers requiring safe. Document SLA implications.

asha: action items:\n- liam: update manifest schema PR with bundle_id, format_version, compatible_loader_min_version, header_schema_uri (owner)\n- mike: implement WeightSource.verify_header and verifier cache + unit tests (owner)\n- sora: design deferred-verify rollback test harness + canary (owner)\n- eva: write deployment knob + KMS key rotation doc (owner)\n- asha: coordinate rollout plan and feature flag gating (owner)

asha: timeline: aim RFC follow-up PRs this week, protos in runtime next sprint. Can we get ownership ack?

mike: ack from me. will spike verifier cache today. :thumbsup:

liam: ack. will PR manifest changes by EOD.

sora: ack. will draft test harness.
eva: ack. will draft KMS runbook + flag.

asha: thanks all. if nobody objects I'll put this in eng-ml RFC follow-up and assign owners.

mike: no objections from infra side. leaning :+1:.

liam: no objections.

sora: one tiny nit: add explicit telemetry event when serving unverified weights so we can alert.

asha: good call — adding telemetry event `weights.unverified_served` to action list.

deploy-bot: NOTE: bumped `prefetch-smoke` timeout to 5s in experimental pipeline for verification runs.

asha: I'll open the follow-up thread with links to PRs once they're up. Thanks! :rocket:
